```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(sf)
  library(fixest)
  library(tmap)
  library(VancouvR)
  library(cancensus)
})
tmap_mode("plot")
```

```{r}
#| label: data
#| include: false
# City of Vancouver street segments, labelled by hundred block. Some labels
# cover a range of blocks, such as "4600-4800 ONTARIO ST".
streets <- get_cov_data("public-streets") |> st_transform(26910)

street_line <- function(name) {
  streets |>
    filter(str_detect(hblock, paste0("^[0-9-]+ ", name, "$"))) |>
    st_union()
}

# Distance to a north-south street, negative on its west side
signed_distance <- function(points, line) {
  link <- st_nearest_points(points, line)
  on_line <- st_coordinates(st_cast(link, "POINT")[c(FALSE, TRUE)])
  dist <- as.numeric(st_length(link))
  if_else(st_coordinates(points)[, 1] < on_line[, 1], -dist, dist)
}

ontario <- street_line("ONTARIO ST")
ontario_box <- st_bbox(ontario)

# 2021 Census tracts, and dissemination areas with median household income
tracts <- get_census("CA21", regions = list(CSD = "5915022"), level = "CT",
                     geo_format = "sf", quiet = TRUE) |>
  select(tract = GeoUID) |>
  st_transform(26910)
das <- get_census("CA21", regions = list(CSD = "5915022"), level = "DA",
                  vectors = c(income = "v_CA21_906"),
                  geo_format = "sf", quiet = TRUE) |>
  select(income) |>
  st_transform(26910)

# Single-family sales, 2001-2025, level with Ontario Street (north to south).
# 2021 sales have no lot size or floor area, so they drop out; lot sizes
# under 1,000 sq ft are recording errors.
sales_sf <- read_rds("data/bca262.rds") |>
  filter(juris_label == "City of Vancouver", act_use_cat == "S/F Res",
         !is.na(lon), price > 100000, between(year(sale_date), 2001, 2025),
         lotsize >= 1000, floorarea > 0) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(26910) |>
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(geometry)[, 2]) |>
  filter(between(y, ontario_box["ymin"], ontario_box["ymax"])) |>
  mutate(dist = signed_distance(geometry, ontario))

n_sales <- nrow(sales_sf)
sales_sf <- sales_sf |>
  st_join(tracts) |>
  st_join(das) |>
  # BC Assessment stopped recording the E/W prefix in 2015, so the side comes
  # from the map. East-west streets are the numbered avenues and King Edward,
  # written "41ST AVE W" in early years and "41ST" later.
  mutate(west = dist < 0,
         ew_street = str_detect(str_name,
                                "^(\\d+(ST|ND|RD|TH)|KING EDWARD)( AVE)?( [EW])?$"),
         year = year(sale_date), quarter = paste(year, quarter(sale_date)),
         age = year - year_built)
stopifnot(nrow(sales_sf) == n_sales)  # a sale on a boundary would appear twice

sales <- st_drop_geometry(sales_sf)
```

```{r}
#| label: models
#| include: false
# West-side premium: log price on west, with size and age, comparing sales in
# the same census tract and quarter. Standard errors clustered by tract.
premium <- function(data, controls = "") {
  f <- as.formula(paste("log(price) ~ west + log(lotsize) + log(floorarea) + age",
                        controls, "| quarter + tract"))
  m <- feols(f, data = data, cluster = ~tract)
  tibble(b = coef(m)[["westTRUE"]], se = se(m)[["westTRUE"]], n = nobs(m))
}
near_ontario <- function(bandwidth) filter(sales, abs(dist) < bandwidth, ew_street)

main <- premium(near_ontario(150))
with_income <- premium(filter(near_ontario(150), !is.na(income)), "+ log(income)")

# Citywide: all sales on each side of the line, without the tract comparison
citywide_model <- feols(log(price) ~ west + log(lotsize) + log(floorarea) + age |
                          quarter, data = sales, cluster = ~tract)
citywide <- tibble(b = coef(citywide_model)[["westTRUE"]],
                   se = se(citywide_model)[["westTRUE"]],
                   n = nobs(citywide_model))

pct <- function(b) 100 * (exp(b) - 1)
```

## Thesis

```{r code-thesis, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models"), eval=FALSE}
```

::: {.key-point}
A house just west of Vancouver's Ontario Street sells for about `r round(pct(main$b))`% more than a similar house just east of it. Buyers pay for the "W" in the address.
:::

- **Evidence:** BC Assessment sales, 2001–2025: `r scales::comma(main$n)` single-family sales within 150 m of Ontario Street.
- **Comparison:** west side against east side, in the same census tract and quarter, with lot size, floor area and age held fixed.

::: {.notes}
Speaker 1 presents slides 2–5; Speaker 2 presents slides 6–10. About 30 seconds. Prestige is usually impossible to price: prestigious neighbourhoods also have better schools, safety and jobs. Ontario Street separates the label from the amenities.
:::

## Only the address changes at Ontario Street

```{r code-map, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "map"), eval=FALSE}
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
```{r}
#| label: map
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 5
# A 1.2 km square in the middle of the sample, along Ontario Street
band <- sales_sf |>
  filter(abs(dist) < 150, ew_street) |>
  mutate(side = if_else(west, "West side", "East side"))
centre <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(band)))
window <- st_bbox(c(xmin = centre[1] - 600, xmax = centre[1] + 600,
                    ymin = centre[2] - 600, ymax = centre[2] + 600),
                  crs = st_crs(26910))

tm_shape(st_crop(streets, window), bbox = window) +
  tm_lines(col = "grey70") +
  tm_shape(st_sf(geometry = ontario)) +
  tm_lines(col = "#c0392b", lwd = 4) +
  tm_shape(band) +
  tm_dots(fill = "side", size = 0.4,
          fill.scale = tm_scale_categorical(values = c("East side" = "#eb6834",
                                                       "West side" = "#2a78d6")),
          fill.legend = tm_legend(title = "", position = tm_pos_in("left", "top"),
                                  bg.color = "white")) +
  tm_layout(frame = FALSE)
```
:::
::: {.column width="52%"}
- A quiet residential street (red) with no physical barrier.
- Not a zoning or census tract boundary.
- On east–west streets, crossing it switches the address from "W" to "E".
- Each dot is a sale within 150 m on an east–west street.
:::
::::

::: footer
BC Assessment sales; City of Vancouver public streets
:::

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute. The map shows one stretch of the street; the analysis uses its whole length.
:::

## Prices fall gradually from west to east, then drop at Ontario

```{r code-gradient, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "gradient"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r}
#| label: gradient
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.4
# Split the city into 250 m north-south strips. Price in each strip relative
# to the strip just west of Ontario Street, holding size, age and quarter fixed.
strips <- sales |>
  filter(abs(dist) < 6000) |>
  mutate(strip = floor(dist / 250) * 250 + 125)
strip_model <- feols(log(price) ~ i(strip, ref = -125) + log(lotsize) +
                       log(floorarea) + age | quarter, data = strips)

broom::tidy(strip_model) |>
  filter(str_starts(term, "strip::")) |>
  transmute(km = as.numeric(str_extract(term, "-?\\d+$")) / 1000, estimate) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(km = -0.125, estimate = 0)) |>
  mutate(side = if_else(km < 0, "West", "East")) |>
  ggplot(aes(km, estimate)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = side), method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
              colour = "#2a78d6", fill = "#c9dcf3") +
  geom_point(colour = "grey25") +
  labs(x = "Distance from Ontario Street (km; west is negative)",
       y = "Log price vs strip just west") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

Each dot is a 250 m strip of the city. The only break is at Ontario Street.

::: footer
Log price on strip, lot size, floor area, age and sale-quarter fixed effects; all single-family sales within 6 km
:::

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute. A sceptic's first question: maybe prices just fall from west to east. They do, gradually, on both sides. At Ontario Street they drop all at once.
:::

## Part of the West Side gap is the label itself

```{r code-main, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models", "main-estimate"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r}
#| label: main-estimate
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.2
bind_rows(Citywide = citywide, `Within 150 m` = main, .id = "comparison") |>
  mutate(comparison = fct_rev(comparison)) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct(b), comparison, colour = comparison)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = pct(b - 1.96 * se), xmax = pct(b + 1.96 * se)),
                  linewidth = 1.2, size = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(round(pct(b)), "%")), nudge_y = 0.3, size = 6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Citywide = "grey50", `Within 150 m` = "#2a78d6"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, NA), labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "West-side price premium, similar houses (95% interval)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18)

east_price <- near_ontario(150) |>
  filter(!west, year >= 2023) |>
  summarise(median(price)) |>
  pull()
```

- **Citywide**, similar west-side houses sell for `r round(pct(citywide$b))`% more. That gap includes better schools, parks and views.
- **Within 150 m**, where those are shared, the label alone is worth `r round(pct(main$b))`%: about `r scales::dollar(east_price * (exp(main$b) - 1), accuracy = 10000)` on the median east-side house sold in 2023–2025.

::: footer
Within 150 m: east–west streets, census tract and sale-quarter fixed effects. Citywide: all sales, sale-quarter fixed effects.
:::

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute.
:::

## Alternative 1: any street would show a jump?

```{r code-placebo, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models", "placebo"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r}
#| label: placebo
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.2
# The same comparison at the residential north-south streets used in the paper.
# Sales within 150 m of Ontario Street are left out so its jump cannot leak in.
placebo_streets <- c("TRIMBLE ST", "CARNARVON ST", "MACKENZIE ST", "MACDONALD ST",
                     "TRAFALGAR ST", "YEW ST", "ARBUTUS ST", "MAPLE ST", "CYPRESS ST",
                     "PINE ST", "ALDER ST", "SPRUCE ST", "LAUREL ST", "HEATHER ST",
                     "COLUMBIA ST", "MANITOBA ST", "PRINCE EDWARD ST",
                     "ST. GEORGE ST", "GLADSTONE ST", "CASSIAR ST", "SKEENA ST")

placebo <- function(name) {
  line <- street_line(name)
  box <- st_bbox(line)
  data <- sales_sf |>
    filter(ew_street, abs(dist) >= 150,
           between(x, box["xmin"] - 200, box["xmax"] + 200),
           between(y, box["ymin"], box["ymax"])) |>
    mutate(dist = signed_distance(geometry, line), west = dist < 0) |>
    st_drop_geometry() |>
    filter(abs(dist) < 150)
  if (nrow(data) < 100) return(NULL)  # too few sales to estimate
  premium(data)
}

placebo_results <- map(set_names(placebo_streets), placebo) |>
  compact() |>
  bind_rows(.id = "street") |>
  bind_rows(mutate(main, street = "ONTARIO ST")) |>
  mutate(street = str_to_title(str_remove(street, " ST$")))

placebo_results |>
  ggplot(aes(reorder(street, b), pct(b), colour = street == "Ontario")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = pct(b - 1.96 * se), ymax = pct(b + 1.96 * se))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#c0392b", `FALSE` = "grey40"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "West-side premium (95% interval)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

If prices jumped at every north–south street, other streets would show similar premiums. None comes close to Ontario Street.

::: footer
`r nrow(placebo_results) - 1` other residential streets with at least 100 sales within 150 m; same regression as the main estimate
:::

::: {.notes}
Speaker 2 takes over here. About 1 minute. This is a placebo test: repeat the analysis where nothing should happen. The largest other premium is `r round(pct(max(placebo_results$b[placebo_results$street != "Ontario"])))`%, at `r placebo_results$street[placebo_results$street != "Ontario"][which.max(placebo_results$b[placebo_results$street != "Ontario"])]` Street.
:::

## Alternative 2: richer neighbours, not the label?

```{r code-income, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models"), eval=FALSE}
```

1. **The alternative:** richer households live on the west side, and buyers pay for rich neighbours, not for the "W".
2. **If it were true:** holding local income fixed would shrink the premium.
3. **What we see:** with each dissemination area's 2021 median household income held fixed, the premium is `r round(pct(with_income$b), 1)`%, against `r round(pct(main$b), 1)`% without it.

::: {.key-point}
The premium is not explained by who lives there now.
:::

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute. Dissemination areas are the smallest census areas, about 400 to 700 people.
:::

## The premium holds under other choices

```{r code-robust, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models", "robustness"), eval=FALSE}
```

```{r}
#| label: robustness
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.8
robustness <- bind_rows(
  `50 m band` = premium(near_ontario(50)),
  `100 m band` = premium(near_ontario(100)),
  `150 m band (baseline)` = main,
  `200 m band` = premium(near_ontario(200)),
  `Standard lots (3,500–4,400 sq ft)` =
    premium(filter(near_ontario(150), between(lotsize, 3500, 4400))),
  `Sales 2001–2008` = premium(filter(near_ontario(150), year <= 2008)),
  `Sales 2009–2016` = premium(filter(near_ontario(150), between(year, 2009, 2016))),
  `Sales 2017–2025` = premium(filter(near_ontario(150), year >= 2017)),
  `With local income` = with_income,
  .id = "check"
)

robustness |>
  mutate(check = fct_rev(fct_inorder(check))) |>
  ggplot(aes(pct(b), check)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = pct(b - 1.96 * se), xmax = pct(b + 1.96 * se)),
                  colour = "#2a78d6") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = \(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = "West-side premium (95% interval)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16)
```

::: footer
Each row repeats the main regression with one choice changed.
:::

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute. The estimate stays between `r round(min(pct(robustness$b)))`% and `r round(max(pct(robustness$b)))`%. The 50 m band is the least precise because it has only `r robustness$n[1]` sales.
:::

## What this analysis cannot tell us

```{r code-limits, ref.label=c("setup", "data", "models"), eval=FALSE}
```

- **Few clusters.** Sales within 150 m fall in only `r n_distinct(near_ontario(150)$tract)` census tracts, so the intervals are approximate.
- **Single-family homes only.** Condo buyers may value the label differently.
- **A local estimate.** It measures the label's value near Ontario Street; elsewhere it may be worth more or less.
- **Unseen differences.** Amenities look the same on both sides, but differences that buyers see and the data do not cannot be fully ruled out.

::: {.notes}
About 1 minute.
:::

## Takeaways

- A neighbourhood's reputation is priced: the "W" is worth about `r round(pct(main$b))`% of a house's price.
- The premium was `r round(pct(robustness$b[6]))`% in 2001–2008 and `r round(pct(robustness$b[8]))`% in 2017–2025, more than a century after the east–west divide began.
- Improving amenities on the east side may not close the gap; reputation persists on its own.

::: {.notes}
About 30 seconds. The paper this example follows began as an in-class presentation by four UBC Sauder undergraduates.
:::

## Backup: Sources

- Larsen, D., S. Lee, and S. H. Lee (2026). "The Value of W: Pricing Neighbourhood Prestige." Working paper, SSRN.
- Heblich, S., A. Trew, and Y. Zylberberg (2021). "East-Side Story: Historical Pollution and Persistent Neighborhood Sorting." *Journal of Political Economy* 129(5): 1508–1552.
- Keele, L. J., and R. Titiunik (2015). "Geographic Boundaries as Regression Discontinuities." *Political Analysis* 23(1): 127–155.
- Data: BC Assessment sales (course file `bca262.rds`); City of Vancouver public streets; Statistics Canada 2021 Census via `cancensus`.

## Backup: Decision log

1. **Side from the map, not the address.** BC Assessment stopped recording the E/W prefix in 2015; filtering on it silently dropped every later sale.
2. **Two street-name formats.** East–west streets appear as "41ST AVE W" in early years and "41ST" later; matching one format lost the other years.
3. **Range-labelled street segments.** Some City segments are labelled "4600-4800 ONTARIO ST"; matching single blocks only left gaps in the southern half of the street.
4. **Placebo samples leave out Ontario Street's band,** so its jump cannot leak into neighbouring streets.
5. **2021 dropped.** The course file has no lot size or floor area for 2021 sales.
